**How it works:**
- **The first line is `/* /* */`.** Rust lets block comments nest, so the inner `/*` opens a second level and the `*/` closes only that one. Everything up to the later `// */` stays a comment in Rust. C++ doesn't nest comments, so for C++ the comment ends on that first line and it compiles the C++ code that follows.
- **For C++, the Rust code is hidden by a backslash.** A line `// \` ends with a backslash, so C++ treats the next line as part of the same comment. That next line holds the whole Rust `fn main`, written on one line. Rust doesn't do this, so for Rust it's just an empty comment followed by real code.
- **Both versions use big-integer arithmetic.** Each number is stored as a list of 9-digit chunks, so large N gives exact results with no overflow.

The program needs N as its first argument. Without one, the C++ version exits with status 1 and the Rust version stops with an error.
